newsitem.title: USA: Fashion king Versace gunned down in Miami.
newsitem.headline: Fashion king Versace gunned down in Miami.

text.p: World-renowned fashion designer Gianni Versace was shot and killed on Tuesday in an execution-style murder in the tourist mecca of Miami Beach.
Police and witnesses said Versace, 50, was shot twice at point-blank range in the back of the head in a "targeted" killing by a lone gunman who immediately fled the scene.
"I believe he was targeted, yes," Miami Beach Police Chief Richard Barreto told a news conference.
"There was apparently no robbery attempt involved."
Police were seeking a white man aged about 25 who approached Versace, a declared homosexual, and shot him as he unlocked the gates of his lavish mansion shortly before 9 a.m. EDT (1300 GMT).

In Washington, a federal law enforcement official said the FBI was looking into the possibility that alleged "spree killer" Andrew Cunanan, a fugitive who is one of America's most wanted men, may have been involved in the killing.

Cunanan, 27, is suspected of four murders including that of his former male lover during a two-week, cross-country killing spree that began in Minneapolis. The FBI said he stole a red pickup truck belonging to his last victim, a New Jersey cemetery caretaker shot to death May 10.
Unconfirmed media reports said such a truck may have been found in a parking garage near the site of the killing, along with discarded clothing of the type worn by the killer.
Asked why the FBI suspected Cunanan may have been involved, the official who declined to be identified replied: "There were witnesses there."
A Miami television station said Cunanan may have been arrested in the area but gave no source for its report. Police had no comment.

Barreto said that police had "a number of suspects". Both he and Miami FBI spokeswoman Anne Figueiras declined to specifically link Cunanan to the killing. The FBI had distributed about 2,000 wanted posters portraying Cunanan in Florida in recent weeks but had sightings of him from around the country.
Versace was openly gay. "That was common knowledge though I don't think he went around saying it," said a writer at Miami's Fashion Spectrum magazine.
South Beach has one of America's most active gay scenes but it was not clear if the killing had any sexual motive.

Philip Villaneuva, the neurosurgeon who treated Versace at Miami's Jackson Memorial Hospital, said the Italian designer was shot twice in the back of the head, once on each side about "2-3 finger breadths" behind the ears.

"It appears there were two entry wounds to the back of the skull. One of the bullets apparently stayed within the skull," he said. "Either one would have been fatal. There was one exit wound next to his nose on the right side."
Villaneuva said he could not tell what type of gun was used because the bullet was too distorted. An autopsy would be carried out.
Barreto at first said a handgun was recovered near the scene but later declined to confirm the find.

Versace, 50, was returning to his home from a nearby restaurant on the glamorous Ocean Drive strip, a street of brightly painted art deco hotels and trendy restaurants frequented by models and featured in the Robin Williams movie "The Bird Cage."
Miami Beach, a narrow finger of land off the Florida mainland, is the centre of Miami's swinging fashion and music industry. It has its own police force and city administration.
Shopowner Eddie Bianchi, 50, told Reuters he was nearby when the shooting occurred.
"We heard two shots. I saw people running. Gianni was on the stairs. He was shot twice in the head. We were trying to help Gianni on the floor, but we realised it was too late."
"Gianni Versace was a worldwide personality, so for the people who work here on Ocean Drive, it's really awful."
People at the scene said the white-haired Versace had walked to the nearby News Cafe, a popular 24-hour restaurant, to buy his morning paper and was shot upon his return home.

Globe-trotting Versace, who dressed some of the world's most beautiful women, was not a permanent resident of Miami Beach but frequently stayed at the white stone mansion, the only private residence on Ocean Drive.
A senior manager at the News Cafe said Versace was his usual gracious self when he walked to the shop to buy magazines on Tuesday morning.

The slaying recalled for many the murder of another Italian fashion czar, Maurizio Gucci, in Milan in 1995. His former wife and two alleged hit men were among five people charged in that killing in February this year.
